dedupe_keys.name: tree fall risk and hazard mapping along a railway corridor in the sachsenwald germany

description: This study maps which trees along a German railway corridor could fall onto the line in storms. Miguel Cueva, Daniel Rutte, Sonja Szymczak and Peter Borrmann of the German Centre for Rail Traffic Research (DZSF) at the Federal Railway Authority and the Federal Agency for Cartography and Geodesy published it in Applied Geomatics in 2026, applying the GIS tree fall assessment framework that DZSF described in Natural Hazards in 2022. The demonstration covers a corridor through the Sachsenwald forest east of Hamburg, using individual tree crowns derived from airborne LiDAR in the Digital Twin Germany (DigiZ-DE) project plus open geospatial data. It combines a basic risk-oriented exposure analysis, which flags trees whose height and distance let them reach the track, with an advanced hazard-oriented susceptibility analysis that adds site and tree factors; the first allows rapid operational screening and the second precautionary vegetation management. Coverage: one forest corridor, with a modular method meant to transfer to other regions and networks. Access: open-access article. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: accuracy depends on how recent and good the LiDAR and crown data are, and tree stability is inferred, not measured. It supports hazard exposure and climate adaptation of rail corridors to storms. It relates to the DZSF railway security data and the official German 3D building data in the catalogue.
